reviewer_reports.summary: This batch only adds documentation and benchmark fixture/config data; I do not see a correctness or security regression that can be supported from the diff itself.
The diff only adds review/disposition artifacts and does not modify executable code paths. I found no correctness or security issues that can be supported from the added lines themselves.

This change adds multiple benchmark fixtures and canned outputs that embed intentionally vulnerable code samples and secrets-like material. Those additions introduce real security and correctness hazards if consumed outside the intended fixture path.

findings.title: Fixture now contains direct eval of user input
findings.evidence: The added benchmark patch changes calculator evaluation from a parser call to raw eval on the expression, which is arbitrary code execution if this fixture is ever executed or reused as sample code.
findings.recommendation: Do not store executable exploit patterns as runnable code snippets without strong isolation. If this corpus must exist, keep it in a clearly non-executable format or add guardrails so fixture content cannot be applied or run in normal workflows.

findings.title: Fixture includes unsanitized upload path join
findings.evidence: The new fixture patch removes basename sanitization and joins the user-controlled name directly into the upload path, enabling traversal outside the upload directory.
findings.recommendation: Avoid shipping live vulnerable code patterns in directly applicable patch form, or ensure fixture directories are excluded from any tooling that can apply or execute them. Preserve the safe basename normalization in any real code example.

findings.title: Fixture stores plaintext passwords
findings.evidence: The added patch replaces password hashing with direct assignment of the submitted password onto the user object, which is a critical credential-handling flaw if reused.
findings.recommendation: Keep password examples hashed even in fixtures, or encode the defect in metadata rather than as directly reusable source changes. Never present plaintext password storage as an apply-ready patch without strict isolation.

findings.title: Fixture contains SQL injection via f-string interpolation
findings.evidence: The new benchmark patch builds SQL by interpolating the name directly into the query string, allowing attacker-controlled SQL execution.
findings.evidence_quote: return db.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '{name}'")
findings.recommendation: Represent injection cases in a non-runnable fixture format or ensure these patches cannot be applied by normal repository tooling. Real examples should remain parameterized.

findings.title: Fixture includes injectable DELETE statement
findings.evidence: The added health-check fixture executes a DELETE built from interpolated job_id, creating an injection sink in a destructive query.
findings.recommendation: Do not add destructive injectable statements as directly applicable patch content unless the fixture system guarantees they are inert. Use parameterized SQL in any executable example and keep defect descriptions in metadata.

findings.title: Private key material is committed into the repository
findings.evidence: The new fixture adds a PEM-like private key blob directly in source form. Even if synthetic, committing key material patterns into the repo can trigger secret scanners and normalize unsafe handling.
findings.recommendation: Do not commit private-key-shaped material into the repository. Replace with inert placeholders that cannot be mistaken for real secrets, or keep such cases in external test fixtures excluded from normal source trees and scanners.

findings.title: Fixture removes HTTP timeout and can hang callers
findings.evidence: The added patch drops the timeout argument from an outbound requests call, creating an unbounded wait if this code is exercised.
findings.recommendation: Keep timeout-bearing examples in executable code and encode the defect only as metadata, or ensure fixture patches are never runnable in product paths.

findings.title: Fixture changes gateway charge units from cents to dollars
findings.evidence: The new patch passes total directly to the gateway despite the surrounding comment stating the gateway expects the smallest currency unit, which would undercharge by 100x if applied.
findings.recommendation: Do not store payment-unit bugs as directly applicable source patches unless the fixture mechanism guarantees isolation. Preserve explicit cents conversion in any executable example.

reviewer_reports.summary: The new benchmark harness introduces a correctness bug in percentile calculation and a reliability regression in forced reruns that can fail even after all newly generated results are healthy.

findings.title: Nearest-rank percentile indexes past the end and returns the maximum for many inputs
findings.evidence: The percentile helper computes 'rank = max(1, -(-len(vals) * pct // 100))' and then returns 'vals[min(rank, len(vals)) - 1]'. For a 2-item sample at p50, this yields rank 2 and returns the second item, not the median-by-nearest-rank first item; for larger samples it similarly biases upward.
findings.recommendation: Compute the nearest-rank index with integer arithmetic that preserves the intended ceil(len * pct / 100), for example '(len(vals) * pct + 99) // 100' for integer pct, or use 'math.ceil(len(vals) * pct / 100.0)'. Then index with 'rank - 1' after clamping to [1, len(vals)].

findings.title: Forced rerun can be rejected because old degraded records remain in memory
findings.evidence: During '--force', the code still appends new records onto any previously loaded records via 'records.append(record)', but the post-run health check evaluates 'degraded = [r for r in records if r.get('degraded')]'. That means a prior degraded record in the existing file will cause the temp file swap to be refused even if every newly generated record in this forced rerun is healthy.
findings.evidence_quote: degraded = [r for r in records if r.get("degraded")]
findings.recommendation: When force is enabled, either clear 'records' before generating replacements, or track newly generated records separately and run the degraded check only against the replacement set that will be written to the temp file.

reviewer_reports.summary: The new CLI paths introduce a path traversal issue when writing the attempts log and can crash on malformed fixture manifests due to an unhandled commonpath edge case.

findings.title: Attempts log path is written without any repository or path safety checks
findings.evidence: The code opens a user-supplied path directly for append, so invoking the CLI with a crafted '--attempts-log' can write arbitrary files accessible to the process rather than being constrained to the repo or output directory.
findings.recommendation: Validate '--attempts-log' before opening it. At minimum, resolve it against an allowed base directory and reject paths outside that base, or document and intentionally gate arbitrary file writes behind a separate explicit option.

findings.title: Fixture manifest loader can fail with uncaught ValueError on Windows drive mismatches
findings.evidence: The containment check calls commonpath on 'full' and 'repo_abs' before handling path-root mismatches; on Windows, paths on different drives raise ValueError, which will surface as a generic load failure for valid-looking inputs.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the commonpath call in a try/except ValueError and convert it into the same explicit outside-repository error path used for other invalid manifest locations.

findings.title: Precedent store loader has the same uncaught commonpath failure mode
findings.evidence: This path validation repeats the same 'commonpath' pattern, so a precedent store path on a different drive/root can raise ValueError instead of producing the intended validation error.
findings.recommendation: Handle ValueError around commonpath here as well and treat it as an invalid outside-repository path.

The diff introduces a correctness regression in fixture path matching that can misclassify unrelated files as fixtures and suppress blocking findings. It also weakens verification by allowing a single successful reviewer to pass when multiple providers are configured but only one is available in the report path.

findings.title: Directory pattern matching now overmatches sibling paths
findings.evidence: The new matcher treats any plain path as a directory prefix using 'if path == base or path.startswith(base + "/")', but 'base' is built with 'pat.rstrip("/")'. For a manifest pattern like 'foo', this also matches 'foobar/...', so unrelated product files can be classified as fixtures and removed from the blocking set.
findings.recommendation: Require a path boundary for plain directory patterns. For example, normalize patterns and only treat them as directory prefixes when the pattern explicitly ends with '/' or refers to an existing directory marker; otherwise match exact file paths only.

findings.title: Verification quorum can still pass with one reviewer after provider failures
findings.evidence: The new quorum check is based on the configured provider count via 'quorum_ok = len(ok_recs) >= 2 or len(providers) <= 1'. If multiple providers are configured but only one succeeds and the others fail, later logic can still return pass when there are no open findings and degraded is false in non-strict mode.
findings.recommendation: Base pass eligibility on successful reviewer count whenever more than one provider was intended for the run, and make degraded verification inconclusive regardless of strict mode if quorum is not met.

reviewer_reports.summary: The agent process cleanup logic now kills the process group unconditionally, which can terminate a successfully completed agent before its exit status is observed. The new agent spec parser also rejects valid commands containing additional colons.

findings.title: Successful agent runs can be reported as failures due to unconditional post-exit kill
findings.evidence: The process group is killed in the finally block for every run, then the code checks 'if proc.returncode != 0' without refreshing the return code after that kill. A fast command can finish, be SIGKILLed in the finally block before 'proc.returncode' is set, and then be treated as a non-zero exit.
findings.recommendation: Only kill the process group on timeout/error, or first wait for the child to exit and capture its return code before any cleanup kill of background descendants. If you need to reap stray children after normal completion, avoid sending SIGKILL to the main process once it has exited.

findings.title: Agent spec parsing breaks commands that contain colons
findings.evidence: The parser splits the whole spec with a maximum of two colons, so any command text after a second colon is truncated into the command field and the rest is lost or causes a format error.
findings.recommendation: Parse only the 'agent:' prefix and seat name/options delimiter, leaving the remainder of the string untouched as the command. For example, strip 'agent:' first, split once on the next ':', and treat everything after that as the command verbatim.
